notes.title: TBAS v1.3.4 Hotfix / Thrustmaster T. Flight Rudder Pedals (TFRP) - WINDOWS ONLY
notes.content: [p]Only one, major fix this time: after a hefty amount of spelunking through Unity documentation, help forums, and tinkering in the game engine, the Thrustmaster T. Flight Rudder Pedals are now supported NATIVELY (out-of-the-box) in TBAS Study Pro. At long last, the previous guide for configuring the TARGET software to get the pedals to work is now OBSOLETE and UNNECESSARY. Unfortunately, this fix is only applicable for PC/Windows systems. I still cannot figure out how to get the pedals (with the USB adapter dongle) to register in MacOS.[/p][p][/p][h2]New Process for Binding the TFRP Pedals:[/h2][p][/p][p]There is a quirk that is worth noting... they work "Out-of-the-box", but ONLY out of the box. You cannot bind the pedals like you would bind any other device. If you have previously bound any other input for the pedals, you must click the "RESET" button beside the Joystick "Pedal" input to get it reset it back to the default of "Slider", and then the TFRP pedals should work without any further hassle as long as you've selected "TRudderJoystickHID" as the Assigned Controller. Please do not hesitate to notify me of any issues you have with this update/getting the pedals to work.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44739542/3211b7e00324a38a80d149f9e3454cb2a5e87ab9.png"][/img][/p][p]As you can see from the above image, the "Pedal" input under "Joystick" has been RESET back to "Slider". It should work by default under this configuration without any further "Binding" needing to be done.[/p]

notes.title: NEW: Online Leaderboards - v1.3 Update
notes.content:
Through the use of the Steam API, Online Leaderboards are now available for TBAS Study Pro.

The Online Leaderboard is accessible either from the Main Menu or the Stats Menu, and lets users compare their performance to their peers. If you ever wanted to know how your performance measures up to the national community, now you can know!

Have a really good score in your save files, and you don't want to go through the effort of running a new assessment to place yourself on the leaderboard? Don't worry! When you select a category in the Online Leaderboard screen, your top score from that category is immediately loaded from your system files to the leaderboards. In other words: if it's available in your Stats screen, it'll be loaded to the Leaderboards!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44739542/1c4076bcd722133e7cfacf3362ea63938c609522.png[/img]
Left-hand Side Selections:
[list]
[*] USAF TBAS: Shows results for the highest overall USAF (TBAS) Assessment scores. This is the default selection.
[*] NAVY ASTB: Shows results for the highest overall Navy (ASTB-E) Assessment scores.
[*] Directional Orientation Test: Shows results for the highest Directional Orientation Test scores. This score will populate whether you completed the Directional Orientation test in the USAF or Navy Assessment Modes.
[*] Multitasking Test: Shows results for the highest Multitasking Test scores, available in the USAF Assessment Mode.
[*] Terrain ID: Shows results for the highest Terrain Identification scores, available in the Navy Assessment Mode.
[*] TBAS and ASTB Aircraft Tracking Test buttons: Shows best scores for Aircraft Tracking test completed via the USAF and Navy Assessments respectively.
[/list]
Right-hand Side Selections:
[*] Local: Displays your position in the global leaderboard, with the 9 people closest in score to you. This is the default selection.
[*] Global: Displays the all-time top 10 performers in TBAS Study Pro. If you're here (and you didn't cheat!), you're practically guaranteed to become a pilot in your service of choice!
[*] Friends: Displays your friends' scores. See how well your scores compare to theirs!

Note: The Online Leaderboards will not populate if you're not logged in to Steam, as they operate through the Steam API. If you're logged into Steam but the leaderboard still is not populating, try restarting the program.

If you ever want to be at the top of the leaderboard, now's the time to log in! Good luck out there, future pilots!

notes.title: TBAS-v1.2.4 / X56 Throttle and Other Input Fixes
notes.content:
[h2]Fixes[/h2]
The following are fixes for the Aircraft Tracking test:
[list]
[*] The "Two Dimensional Throttle" Toggle (a compatibility setting for Logitech X56 HOTAS Throttles) in the Rebind Menu had broken in a previous update, and has now been fixed.
[*] New controller bindings set in the Rebind Menu had failed to take effect until the Aircraft Tracking test was restarted. Because I suspect this problem is with Unity's "Rebind" feature, I have a "Apply Settings Now?" pop-up that will appear when exiting out of the rebind menu. Pressing "Yes" will Restart the Aircraft Tracking portion of the test from the beginning, while selecting "No" will cause all changes to take effect whenever the test is reloaded.
[*] By default, the "Right Alt" key ("Right Option" key on Mac) is used to skip tutorial segments. There was a bug whereby if the "Right Alt" key was pressed during the "Emergency Test Tutorial" portion of the Navy ASTB assessment that the assessment would end prematurely. This has been fixed and now simply skips the tutorial as expected.
[/list]

Finally, the Directional Orientation test (UAV Test) had a bug whereby if a user made selections too quickly that the test could continue forever. That has been fixed as well.

These bug fixes come courtesy of the great users (like you!) who notified me of them. If you notice something amiss, please do not hesitate to alert me of the issue!

notes.title: TBAS v1.2.3 / Removing Controller Autoswitching
notes.content:
[h2]Changes[/h2]
In the previous update I had re-added auto-switching for controller inputs allowing players to control TBAS Study Pro "out of the box" (without needing to fiddle with the rebinding menu), allowing Unity to automatically switch "active" input to be whatever controller was sending signals to the computer. However, I was contacted about an issue from multiple users where certain controllers would provide a continuous input to Unity (e.g. stick drift) regardless of user intent, thereby interfering with alternative/intentional user input. This frustrated users, and I don't want users to have to play the "deduction-game" on what controller is interfering with their intended input the first time they boot up the program. Because of this, I have removed input auto-switching again, but this time the UI in the Aircraft Tracking test has been rearranged to more specifically guide users to explicitly assign controllers to tests/rebind inputs if they haven't yet done so. It's not a perfect solution, but it's the best I can come up with given the contraints that the Unity game engine provides.

notes.title: TBAS Study Pro v1.2.2 Patch / Changes to Dichotic Listening and Emergency

[*] Dichotic Listening Test "Even" and "Odd" inputs can now be triggered from two different controllers via new "Manual Rebinding" options
[*] Emergency Test "Power", "Fuel", and "Reset" inputs can now be triggered from multiple different controllers via new "Manual Rebinding" options
[*] Emergency Test "Power" and "Fuel" inputs can now be set to be an "Axis" (such as a dial) or "Positive/Negative" (one button for "down", another button for "up") style inputs.

[*] Without "Manual Rebinding" toggled, the program should automatically detect the controller that the current player intends to use by which controller is currently sending inputs to the program. This functionality became broken in the update that added support for the Thrustmaster 16000M Throttle, but has now been restored.
[/list]

notes.title: NEW: Terrain Identification Subtest - v1.2 Update
notes.content:
[h1]Terrain Identification Subtest (Navy/ASTB-E/PBMB)[/h1]
[list]
[*] Within 35 seconds, find the compass-orientation of a UAV looking down at terrain below by comparing the terrain in its point-of-view with a North-oriented map on the left-hand side of the screen
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44739542/101f501b6e6b331ee3e80af7b93267730cd0dc6e.png[/img]
[*] Having trouble getting the hang of things? Try the comprehensive tutorial anytime to refresh yourself on the problem-solving process
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44739542/2a20676ad9910b72d65c9198a59e3c6e8bf71212.png[/img]
[*] Are you practicing, and you're not sure why some of your answers are showing as "WRONG"? Check the Terrain Identification "Pause" menu to compare your previous selection with the previous correct answer
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44739542/91a022e450f5d04ac22dd36621936436501959cb.png[/img]
[*] Want to practice the PBMB part of the ASTB-E as if you were taking the real thing? The Navy Assessment mode is now updated to include a "Assessment Mode" version of the Terrain Identification subtest
[/list]

[h2]Minor Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] New "Stats" Menu Save File Delete Buttons: Previous assessment save files in the "Stats" menu can now be deleted via "Delete All" and "Delete Selected" buttons. This was added because there is a rare bug where save files can get corrupted, and the only possible fix is to delete the offending files. These new options allow the user to delete corrupted save files without having to dig through their file system to find them.
[*] Rebalanced Assessment Scoring: I noticed that it was possible to achieve decent scores in certain subtests in the previous versions of TBAS Study Pro by doing absolutely nothing. As a result, I have rebalanced Assessment Scoring to be less forgiving. You may notice that your Assessment scores are lower than before, and that's intentional.
[/list]

Be aware: Due to the addition of the new Terrain Identification subtest, old Navy/ASTB-E/PBMB save files may have display issues in the new version of TBAS Study Pro. There should be no critical compatibility issues, but if any are to arise, simply utilize the new "Delete" buttons to clear out old Stat menu save files.

[h2]FUTURE PLANS[/h2]
Previously I had mentioned the creation of "Custom Assessments" and an "Updated Stats Screen" as a part of a potential future "v1.2" update. Well, this is v1.2 and those features are still not available. This is because I no longer believe those features would meaningfully enhance the user experience relative to the amount of work required to build them, especially when considering that doing so would only draw my attention away from my other software projects that are far more pressing. Right now, my priorities concerning the future of TBAS Study Pro are in making sure I meet the needs of my users (YOU!) by only adding things I know for a fact are needed, like this Terrain Identification subtest (added per user request), or expanding accessibility options (see, for reference, the past few controller and bug-fix-focused updates). If you want to see something in TBAS Study Pro, please do not hesitate to reach out to me to request it! My plan has been and always will be to provide the ultimate TBAS preparatory tool, and if there's anything I can do to bring TBAS Study Pro closer to that goal I will do my best to make it so.

If you have any feedback, the best way to reach me is via the [url=https://discord.gg/HvuWjSapvr]TBAS Study Pro Discord Server[/url].

You can also reach me via Steam messenger or the Steam Discussion forum, but I don't receive notifications from posts in the Discussion forums so that method of contact is less effective.

Thank you for all your support, and good luck on the TBAS and ASTB!

Just a small update this week:

Main Addition - Per user-request, added support explicitly for the Logitech Pro Flight X56 Rhino HOTAS throttle controller. notes.title: HOTFIX - Added Toggle in Main Menu Settings for UI Navigation Using Controllers
notes.content: Added settings toggle to the Main Menu for enabling/disabling UI navigation via controllers (gamepads, throttles, and joysticks). Controller UI navigation is now "Off" by default, meaning users will only be able to use Mouse and Keyboard to navigate menus unless they explicitly choose to enable the UI navigation using controllers feature. This should prevent the issues whereby players will have a Throttle or some other kind of input device plugged in that will send UI navigation commands to TBAS Study Pro, overriding UI input from the mouse and keyboard (which users are much more likely to be using), and make for a better user experience.

notes.title: TBAS Study Pro v1.1 - Universal Rebind, Bugfixes, and More
notes.content:
All the new features and fixes from the TBAS Study Pro beta have been pushed to the main version! While you can continue to use the "beta" version, there are no new beta updates planned for the near future unless any bugs are reported/fixed.

If you have been using the beta, none of these features will be new to you. However, to recap all the changes over the past two months:

NEW MAJOR FEATURES

TOTAL INPUT REBINDING SUPPORT:
While the Aircraft Tracking test only supports keyboard/mouse, XBOX/PS5 controllers, and the Thrustmaster HOTAS Full Kit X combination joystick/pedals by default, with this update you should be able to rebind inputs from any joystick controller to any action in the Aircraft Tracking test, as long as the Unity game engine supports it. (Issues with specific controller compatibility will be met on a case-by-case basis through forum-posts or on the Discord)

MULTIPLE SIMULTANEOUS CONTROLLER INPUT SUPPORT - MANUALLY BIND CONTROLLERS TO TESTS:
If you are using multiple different controllers simultaneously (e.g. a standalone joystick and a standalone rudder pedal set, each with their own USB cable), you can enable "Manually Bind Controllers To Tests" to assign each of your controllers to whatever test you wish those controllers to be solely responsible for. If this is left disabled, TBAS Study Pro will handle all controller inputs automatically, but using more than one controller simultaneously will result in an input conflict. Note: Enabling it will default all UI input handling to your Keyboard/Mouse to prevent soft-locking the program.

All of these features are accessible via the Settings/Pause menu of the Aircraft Tracking test, and apply only to the Aircraft Tracking test. All other tests still support only Keyboard/Mouse.

MINOR FEATURES AND CHANGES
[list]
[*] "Title Screen" buttons replaced with "Menu Screen" buttons that take you to the main menu instead of the title screen (for ease of navigation).
[*] "Exit" buttons placed in every pause menu on every test, so that you don't have to go to the main menu every time you wish to exit the program.
[*] Small video previews of each test appear in the main menu when selecting a test, but before confirming selection.
[*] Estimated time of completion for TBAS and PBMB assessment modes.
[*] "Are You Sure?" Prompt added when "EXIT" is selected.
[*] Various other minor quality-of-life improvements
[/list]

BUGS THAT WERE FIXED
[list]
[*] Directional Orientation: After running the tutorial, the first question is incorrect.
[*] Directional Orientation: "Easy Mode" button text changes to reflect if Easy Mode is activated.
[*] MULTITASKING: The radio segment has a 1/4 chance of incorrectly grading an answer as "Incorrect" or "Correct".
[*] MULTITASKING: "Percent Correct" stats tracking in the pause menu incorrect or not operating properly.
[*] AIRCRAFT TRACKING: "Test Activation" screen wipes all selected modes when pulled up.
[*] Text wrapping fixed on certain elements of the Stats screen.
[*] Various other minor bugs and fixes.
[/list]

FUTURE PLANS
With the release of v1.1, I feel that TBAS Study Pro is in a stable enough state to meet the needs of the majority of the userbase. I will not be making any updates any time soon except in response to bug reports or minor feature requests. However, at some point in the future I would like to add the following features:
[list]
[*] Custom Assessments: Users would be able to select from a list of tests that they could arrange in any order to compile into a "Custom Assessment", with a custom time limit for each test. The "USAF Assessment" and "PBMB Assessment" options would still be available, but as "Presets" that would preload the Custom Assessment screen with the tests and times that are used in the real TBAS or PBMB (according to publicly available information, or according to a guesstimate, just as the current modes are set up).
[*] Updated Stats Screen: The stats screen would be updated to be a lot more robust, allowing for a further breakdown of assessment performances such as graphs showing rates of improvement, common errors you've made (i.e. areas of improvement), etc.
[/list]
There is no guarantee that I'll actually have time to publish these features as a part of "v1.2", but if I do ever ship another major update it will be focused on those changes.

THANK YOU ALL FOR YOUR SUPPORT

If you are having any difficulty using or accessing features of the new update or are experiencing any bugs, do not hesitate to reach out to me. My plan has been and always will be to provide the ultimate TBAS preparatory tool, and if there's anything I can do to bring TBAS Study Pro closer to that goal I will do it.

notes.title: Thrustmaster TFRP Rudder Pedals Config Guide + Hotfix / Minor Bug Fixes
notes.content:
[h2]IMPORTANT UPDATE - V1.3.4 AND UP (2025-06-23):[/h2][p][/p][p]In v1.3.4 update (and later), the process below will still work but is NO LONGER NECESSARY and is OBSOLETE. To get the Thrustmaster T. Flight Rudder Pedals (TFRP) to work all you need to do is to set "TRudderJoystickHID" as the assigned controller and click the "Reset" button beside the "Pedal" input binding button (it should read as "Slider") and the TFRP pedals should work from then on without further hassle. See the link to the community post [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2673460/view/510709651799540189?l=english"]here[/url].[/p][p][/p][h2]In V1.3.3 and Earlier:[/h2][p][/p][p]The Issue:  By default, Thrustmaster TFRP Rudder Pedals do not work when not as a part of the Thrustmaster T. Flight Full Kit setup (i.e. they do not work when used as a separate controller with they're own USB cable); This is because the game engine that TBAS Study Pro is built on fundamentally does not recognize/support certain inputs from the TFRP pedals when used with its own USB cable.[/p][p][/p][p]The Fix/Workaround:  [/p][olist][*][p]Install Thrustmaster's official "TARGET" software using this [url="https://support.thrustmaster.com/en/product/tfrp-en/"]link[/url] (If the link does not work, the URL may have changed).
[/p][/*][*][p]Once the TARGET software is installed, open the "TARGET GUI" program and select "NEW CONFIGURATION".[/p][p][/p][/*][*][p] On the following pop-up, give a name to the new configuration file (such as "TFRP"), select "BASIC" as the "Type", create a folder where you want the configuration file to be stored, and click "OK"
[/p][/*][*][p] On the following screen, scroll to the right until you see the "TFRP Rudder" pedal listed. Select them and click "NEXT".
[/p][/*][*][p] On the following screen, from the drop-downs, set "TRPRIGHT" to "NONE", "TRUDDER" to "DX_SLIDER_AXIS", and "TRPLEFT" to "NONE", then click "NEXT".
[/p][/*][*][p] On the following screen, click "SAVE". This will create your configuration file (with the ".fcf" extension) in the folder you selected for the file to be stored.
[/p][/*][*][p] You can either select "Run Configuration" on this screen, or click "Finish"/"Exit to Dashboard" and select "Run Configuration" from the following screen. On the Browse window that appears, select your configuration file (.fcf). While the configuration is running your TFRP controller identifier will be replaced with "HID:44F-FFFF". This is how it will appear in the Rebind menu in TBAS Study Pro.  [/p][p][/p][p]Note! - If something in the nature of "TRudderJoystickHID" still appears alongside or instead of "HID:44F-FFFF" the process WILL NOT WORK, and you must close TBAS Study Pro, restart TARGET, and try running the configuration again before restarting TBAS Study Pro. Additionally, the configuration must be running BEFORE you start TBAS Study Pro, otherwise it may recognize the old input and ONLY the old input. If restarting TBAS Study Pro does not get "TRudderJoystickHID" to be replaced by "HID:44F-FFFF", then try restarting your computer instead. [/p][p][/p][/*][*][p] In TBAS Study Pro, in the Aircraft Tracking Test, in the REBIND CONTROLS menu cycle through the available "PEDAL CONTROLLER" inputs until you see "HID:44F-FFFF"; this should have replaced your normal TFRP Rudder Pedal input, and you should not be able to select TFRP Rudder Pedals instead of "HID:44F-FFFF" as a kind of input while the TARGET configuration is running.[/p][p][/p][/*][*][p] Under "Joystick Bindings", select the input for "PEDAL" and move your pedals until it registers "Z", "Slider", or "HatSwitch" as the input. If it registers anything else, that may be because it's registering inputs from either other controllers or from the TFRP left or right "Toe Brake" (Stick/X or Stick/Y) (toe brake inputs should be disabled anyway when running your configuration if you set "TRPRIGHT" and "TRPLEFT" to "NONE"). You can get passed input issues by repeatedly attempting to get the pedals to register as "Z", "Slider", or "HatSwitch" (while avoiding putting pressure on the toe-brake), or by simply disabling the Toe Brake inputs in your TARGET software configuration.[/p][p][/p][p]Note! - If you attempt to bind an input to "PEDAL" but nothing happens (the program doesn't receive any input) and your assigned controller is in fact listed as "HID:44F-FFFF", you must set the input to some other controller (such as "Keyboard" or "Mouse"), and then restart TBAS Study Pro. Once TBAS Study Pro has restarted, repeat Steps 8-9. If you are still not receiving any input, check to make sure that the TARGET profile is actually registering input by checking the "DEVICE ANALYZER" window, accessible from the TARGET profile window. If no movement is detected there, set the TBAS Study Pro input to "Keyboard" or "Mouse" again, close TBAS Study Pro, restart the TARGET profile until you see your rudder pedal movement register in the TARGET Device Analyzer window (you may also want to double check that your TARGET profile is configured properly), and then boot up TBAS Study Pro again to repeat Steps 8-9.[/p][/*][/olist][p]
After following all of these steps, TBAS Study Pro should register your pedal inputs as you would expect.

NOTE: If the TARGET software does not register your Pedals as even connected, or when following these steps something doesn't work, please ensure that, on your RJ12 USB adapter, your mode-select switch is switched from "CAR" to "AIRPLANE" mode because TARGET will not be able to reconfigure your pedals otherwise. Additionally, make sure the TARGET reconfigured controller profile is fully timed-in before running TBAS Study Pro. If anything does not work at first, try restarting TBAS Study Pro or backing out of the Aircraft Tracking practice test screen and re-entering it. You may also need to restart your computer entirely to get the TARGET "HID:44F-FFFF" input to replace the old "TRudderJoystickHID" input, as the the old input may be cached and otherwise unreplaceable until the computer has restarted.[/p]

notes.title: Universal Controller Support - Controls Rebinding Update BETA is Live
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44739542/b11f4ebbaa33bf047e7d211ff504ec92e104b755.png[/img]

The beta for the Universal Controller Support update is now live!

[h2]NEW MAJOR FEATURES[/h2]

[h3]TOTAL INPUT REBINDING SUPPORT:[/h3] While the Aircraft Tracking test only supports keyboard/mouse, XBOX/PS5 controllers, and the Thrustmaster HOTAS X joystick and pedals by default, with this update you can rebind inputs from any joystick controller to any action in the Aircraft Tracking test.

[h3]MULTIPLE SIMULTANEOUS CONTROLLER INPUT SUPPORT - MANUALLY BIND CONTROLLERS TO TESTS:[/h3] If you are using multiple different controllers simultaneously (e.g. a standalone joystick and a standalone rudder pedal set, each with their own USB cable), you can enable "Manually Bind Controllers To Tests" to assign each of your controllers to whatever test you wish those controllers to be solely responsible for. If this is left disabled, TBAS Study Pro will handle all controller inputs automatically, but using more than one controller simultaneously will result in an input conflict. Note: Enabling it will default all UI input handling to your Keyboard/Mouse to prevent soft-locking the program.

All of these features are accessible via the Settings/Pause menu of the Aircraft Tracking test, and apply only to the Aircraft Tracking test. All other tests still support only Keyboard/Mouse.

[h2]MINOR FEATURES AND CHANGES[/h2]
[list]
[*] "Title Screen" buttons replaced with "Menu Screen" buttons that take you to the main menu instead of the title screen (for ease of navigation).
[*] "Exit" buttons placed in every pause menu on every test, so that you don't have to go to the main menu every time you wish to exit the program.
[*] Small video previews of each test appear in the main menu when selecting a test, but before confirming selection.
[*] Estimated time of completion for TBAS and PBMB assessment modes.
[*] Some minor bugfixes here and there.
[/list]

[h2]HOW TO GET ACCESS:[/h2]

You can access the beta in Steam right now by right-clicking the game in your library -> selecting "Properties" -> in the window that opens, selecting "Betas" -> beside "Beta Participation" clicking the dropdown and selecting "TBAS Study Pro v1.01 update beta"

Updating the game will then download the update beta.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44739542/3cf74f8a4438422c0c893675640629656fa1f7db.png[/img]

[h2]WHAT NOW?[/h2]

As of now, I will continue to support TBAS Study Pro and make bugfixes and feature changes as long as I am made aware of bugs and features to change by members of the community (YOU!). I cannot guarantee a release date for bringing the update out of beta, but when I feel like it's in a release-ready state, I will release it. My goal is to make this program the ultimate TBAS preparatory tool, and as long as you feel it falls short of that, I will work to make it fit your needs.

notes.title: TBAS Study Pro Official Release
notes.content:
After 6 months of working on this program, the ultimate tool for preparing for the Performance Based Measurement Battery (PBMB) or Test of Basic Aviation Skills (TBAS) is finally released! The first version of this program comes with a variety of features:

[list]
[*] Directional Orientation Test Practice: Improve your directional awareness! Present in the TBAS and PBMB.
[*] Multitasking Test Practice: Improve your memory, fast math, and overall multitasking ability! A test present in the TBAS.
[*] Aircraft Tracking Test Practice: Improve your ability to track multiple objects and respond to prompts simultaneously! Currently supports Thrustmaster HOTAS Joystick and Rudder Pedals, as well as keyboard and select controllers! The Aircraft Tracking tests features 5 sub-tests: Reticle Tracking (Present in TBAS & PBMB), Pedal Tracking (TBAS), Throttle Tracking (PBMB), Listening Test (PBMB), and Emergency Test (PBMB). You can practice these tests individually, or simultaneously with other tests in the "Mode Select" menu.
[*] Comprehensive Tutorials: This program makes it as easy as possible to go in blind, and quickly get a feel for the mechanics of each test.
[*] TBAS and PBMB Assessment Modes: Built from publicly available information on the mechanisms of the real TBAS and PBMB, the Assessment Modes play select tests together in sequence and score your performance on them, as if you were taking the real thing.
[*] History Statistics: View your performance improvement across various assessments in the "Stats" screen. In the screen will be information such as the date of previous assessments, your scores, and which scores on which test sub-components were your all-time best. 
[/list]

This tool aims to be the first and final destination for all of your TBAS or PBMB preparation needs. There are updates in the works to refine the look and feel of the program, as well as adding more controller support at the community's request. If you feel the program is missing something (e.g. more supported joysticks/controllers or more options), suggest a feature in the TBAS Study Pro Steam Community Hub page and I will do my best to respond.
